deadlines.what_en: Pay the acknowledged debt in one payment; passed without payment
Pay within the 7 days given in the notice to pay served on 1 Oct 2026; passed without payment, which opened the way to the payment-order application
deadlines.basis_en: 7 days from service on 2026-10-01, the day of service not counted (Civil Procedure Law Art. 12); 8 Oct 2026 is a Thursday, so no holiday extension

Interest at 5% a year from the date of the application until payment

key_facts.fact_en: Three invoices total AED 318,450 (126,000 + 104,250 + 88,200); after the AED 25,000 credit note for returned goods the net debt is AED 293,450
The debtor acknowledged the debt in writing on 6 Aug 2026 (signed by its general manager, with the company stamp) and promised one payment by 31 Aug 2026
On the acknowledgment the printed amount 318,450 is struck through and corrected by hand to 293,450, initialled و.خ; the corrected figure matches the net debt on page 1 and the amount claimed
The notice to pay, served through the notary public on 1 Oct 2026, gave 7 days, more than the 5-day minimum in Article 144(1); the application was filed on 12 Oct 2026, after that period
The application relies on Article 143 (debt in writing, due, a fixed sum of money) and Article 144 (prior notice to pay; order within 3 working days of filing) of the Civil Procedure Law

citations.note_en: Clause 1: prior notice to pay within at least 5 days. The same sentence refers to clause 4 of the same article (the order issues within 3 working days of filing).

reader_should_flag: On the acknowledgment of debt (page 2) the printed amount AED 318,450 is struck through and corrected by hand to AED 293,450, initialled و.خ (the general manager, Wael Jamal Al Khatib). The application claims the corrected AED 293,450, so the claim rests on a handwritten correction.

The notice to pay was served on 1 Oct 2026 with 7 days to pay; the period ended on 8 Oct 2026, a date computed from the notice and printed nowhere. The application of 12 Oct 2026 came after it ended, as Article 144(1) requires.
